statement: A constant sample attains the saturated likelihood, including at count zero.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h : ℕ} (c : ℕ) : likelihood c c c (fun _ : Fin h ↦ c) = 1 ∧ ∀ K N k, likelihood K N k (fun _ : Fin h ↦ c) ≤ likelihood c c c (fun _ : Fin h ↦ c)

statement: Every saturated urn for a nonempty constant sample. A zero sample permits either design count to vanish. At a positive count one design margin occupies the whole population and the other equals the observed count.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h K N k c : ℕ} (hh : 0 < h) : likelihood K N k (fun _ : Fin h ↦ c) = 1 ↔ K ≤ N ∧ k ≤ N ∧ ((c = 0 ∧ (K = 0 ∨ k = 0)) ∨ (K = N ∧ k = c) ∨ (k = N ∧ K = c))
dossier_scope_note: Constant branch of the all-free maximizer-set claim.

statement: A fixed population admits the observations exactly when twice every observed count is at most the population plus every observed count.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h N : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) : (∃ K k, K ≤ N ∧ k ≤ N ∧ ∀ i, Compatible K N k (x i)) ↔ ∀ i j, 2 * x i ≤ N + x j

statement: At fixed population the compatible design grid is finite, so every nonempty grid attains its maximum. The inequality includes every tied design.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h N : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) : (({p : ℕ × ℕ | p.1 ≤ N ∧ p.2 ≤ N ∧ ∀ i, Compatible p.1 N p.2 (x i)} : Set (ℕ × ℕ))).Finite ∧ ((∃ K k, K ≤ N ∧ k ≤ N ∧ (∀ i, Compatible K N k (x i)) ∧ ∀ J j, J ≤ N → j ≤ N → (∀ i, Compatible J N j (x i)) → likelihood J N j x ≤ likelihood K N k x) ↔ ∀ i j, 2 * x i ≤ N + x j)

statement: With fixed draws and a convergent marked fraction, the sample likelihood converges to the corresponding binomial face, including both point masses.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) (k : ℕ) {A N : ℕ → ℕ} {p : ℝ} (hp : p ∈ Icc 0 1) (hN : Tendsto N atTop atTop) (hA : ∀ᶠ t in atTop, A t ≤ N t) (hAN : Tendsto (fun t ↦ (A t : ℝ) / N t) atTop (𝓝 p)) : Tendsto (fun t ↦ likelihood (A t) (N t) k x) atTop (𝓝 (∏ i, binomialFace k (x i) p))

statement: Swapping the two design counts gives the fixed-composition binomial limit.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) (K : ℕ) {A N : ℕ → ℕ} {p : ℝ} (hp : p ∈ Icc 0 1) (hN : Tendsto N atTop atTop) (hA : ∀ᶠ t in atTop, A t ≤ N t) (hAN : Tendsto (fun t ↦ (A t : ℝ) / N t) atTop (𝓝 p)) : Tendsto (fun t ↦ likelihood K (N t) (A t) x) atTop (𝓝 (∏ i, binomialFace K (x i) p))

statement: With draws held, a finite compatible urn strictly above every compatible binomial height implies finite attainment.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h K₀ N₀ : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) (k : ℕ) (hK₀ : K₀ ≤ N₀) (hk₀ : k ≤ N₀) (hx : ∀ i, Compatible K₀ N₀ k (x i)) (hC : ∀ p ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, (∏ i, binomialFace k (x i) p) < likelihood K₀ N₀ k x) : ∃ K N, K ≤ N ∧ k ≤ N ∧ (∀ i, Compatible K N k (x i)) ∧ ∀ J M, J ≤ M → k ≤ M → (∀ i, Compatible J M k (x i)) → likelihood J M k x ≤ likelihood K N k x

statement: Fixed composition inherits the finite attainment criterion by symmetry.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h k₀ N₀ : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) (K : ℕ) (hK₀ : K ≤ N₀) (hk₀ : k₀ ≤ N₀) (hx : ∀ i, Compatible K N₀ k₀ (x i)) (hC : ∀ p ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, (∏ i, binomialFace K (x i) p) < likelihood K N₀ k₀ x) : ∃ k N, k ≤ N ∧ K ≤ N ∧ (∀ i, Compatible K N k (x i)) ∧ ∀ j M, j ≤ M → K ≤ M → (∀ i, Compatible K M j (x i)) → likelihood K M j x ≤ likelihood K N k x

statement: Each binomial probability in the closed unit interval is reached by a sequence of compatible urns, including both degenerate probabilities.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) (k : ℕ) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ k) {p : ℝ} (hp : p ∈ Icc 0 1) : ∃ A N : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto N atTop atTop ∧ (∀ t i, Compatible (A t) (N t) k (x i)) ∧ Tendsto (fun t ↦ (A t : ℝ)/N t) atTop (𝓝 p) ∧ Tendsto (fun t ↦ likelihood (A t) (N t) k x) atTop (𝓝 (∏ i, binomialFace k (x i) p))

statement: The marked-count hold has the same compatible closed binomial paths by exchanging the design counts.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) (K : ℕ) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ K) {p : ℝ} (hp : p ∈ Icc 0 1) : ∃ k N : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto N atTop atTop ∧ (∀ t i, Compatible K (N t) (k t) (x i)) ∧ Tendsto (fun t ↦ (k t : ℝ)/N t) atTop (𝓝 p) ∧ Tendsto (fun t ↦ likelihood K (N t) (k t) x) atTop (𝓝 (∏ i, binomialFace K (x i) p))

statement: The observation-wise Poisson envelope used in the all-free tail argument. The expression keeps the exact two design depletions.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {K N k c : ℕ} (hc : Compatible K N k c) (hN : c < N) : let lam := (K : ℝ)*k/N mass K N k c ≤ lam^c / ((c.factorial : ℝ)*(1-(c : ℝ)/N)^c) * exp (-(((K : ℝ)-c)*((k : ℝ)-c)/(N : ℝ)))
dossier_scope_note: Observation-wise bound. The optimized uniform all-free cutoff is separate.

statement: A constant sample attains likelihood one at the all-white urn with population and stopping count equal to the common observation.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h : ℕ} (c : ℕ) : totalLikelihood (fun _ : Fin h ↦ c) c c c = 1 ∧ ∀ N m r, totalLikelihood (fun _ : Fin h ↦ c) N m r ≤ 1

statement: A sample containing both zero and a positive number of draws is infeasible.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) {i j : Fin h} (hi : x i = 0) (hj : 0 < x j) : ¬ ∃ N m r, ∀ k, Compatible N m r (x k)
dossier_scope_note: Mixed zero and positive branch only.

statement: The saturated set on constants consists precisely of all zero-stopping urns on zeros, and all-white urns with stopping count equal to the common positive observation otherwise.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h : ℕ} (hh : 0 < h) (N m r c : ℕ) : totalLikelihood (fun _ : Fin h ↦ c) N m r = 1 ↔ m ≤ N ∧ r ≤ m ∧ r = c ∧ (c = 0 ∨ m = N)
dossier_scope_note: Constant branch of the all-free maximizer-set claim.

statement: A fixed population admits precisely all-zero samples and samples whose observations are all positive and at most the population.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h N : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) : (∃ m r, m ≤ N ∧ r ≤ m ∧ ∀ i, Compatible N m r (x i)) ↔ (∀ i, x i = 0) ∨ (∀ i, 0 < x i ∧ x i ≤ N)

statement: At known population the feasible composition and stopping grid is finite. Attainment is equivalent to the explicit data compatibility test.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h N : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) : let D : Set (ℕ × ℕ) := {p | p.1 ≤ N ∧ p.2 ≤ p.1 ∧ ∀ i, Compatible N p.1 p.2 (x i)} D.Finite ∧ (((∀ i, x i = 0) ∨ (∀ i, 0 < x i ∧ x i ≤ N)) ↔ ∃ p ∈ D, IsMaxOn (fun q ↦ totalLikelihood x N q.1 q.2) D p)

statement: At known population and composition the finite stopping-count set attains exactly when it is nonempty.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h N m : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) : let D : Set (ℕ × ℕ) := {p | p.1 ≤ N ∧ p.2 ≤ p.1 ∧ p.1 = m ∧ ∀ i, Compatible N p.1 p.2 (x i)} D.Finite ∧ (D.Nonempty ↔ ∃ p ∈ D, IsMaxOn (fun q ↦ totalLikelihood x N q.1 q.2) D p)

statement: At known population and stopping count the finite composition set attains exactly when it is nonempty.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h N r : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) : let D : Set (ℕ × ℕ) := {p | p.1 ≤ N ∧ p.2 ≤ p.1 ∧ p.2 = r ∧ ∀ i, Compatible N p.1 p.2 (x i)} D.Finite ∧ (D.Nonempty ↔ ∃ p ∈ D, IsMaxOn (fun q ↦ totalLikelihood x N q.1 q.2) D p)

statement: With positive stopping count and held composition, the black count can be optimized by the first crossing. The successor is retained exactly when the adjacent likelihoods tie.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h m r : ℕ} (hh : 0 < h) (x : Fin h → ℕ) (hr : 0 < r) (hm : r ≤ m) (hx : ∀ i, r ≤ x i) : let y := fun i ↦ x i-r let D := Ici (maxBlackDraws y) ∃ b ∈ D, whiteRatio r m (m+b+1) y ≤ 1 ∧ (∀ j ∈ D, j < b → 1 < whiteRatio r m (m+j+1) y) ∧ ∀ j, (IsMaxOn (fun n ↦ totalLikelihood x (m+n) m r) D j ∧ j ∈ D) ↔ j = b ∨ (j = b+1 ∧ whiteRatio r m (m+b+1) y = 1)
dossier_scope_note: Positive stopping count. See the compatible-zero and flatness results for zero stopping count.

statement: When the held stopping count is zero, compatibility requires all observations to be zero and every population above the held composition ties.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h m : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) : (∃ N ≥ m, ∀ i, Compatible N m 0 (x i)) ↔ ∀ i, x i = 0

statement: On compatible zeros with the stopping count held at zero, the likelihood equals one throughout the population ray.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h N m : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) (hm : m ≤ N) (hx : ∀ i, x i = 0) : totalLikelihood x N m 0 = 1

statement: With positive stopping count and composition held, the likelihood vanishes along the population ray.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h m r : ℕ} (hh : 0 < h) (x : Fin h → ℕ) (hr : 0 < r) (hm : r ≤ m) : Tendsto (fun b : ℕ ↦ totalLikelihood x (m+b) m r) atTop (𝓝 0)

statement: With composition held, positive data have a finite population cutoff against any positive likelihood witness, uniformly over feasible stopping counts.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h m : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) (hx : ∃ i, 0 < x i) {C : ℝ} (hC : 0 < C) : ∃ B : ℕ, ∀ N ≥ B, ∀ r, (∀ i, Compatible N m r (x i)) → totalLikelihood x N m r < C

statement: With composition held, every feasible sample attains a maximum. The zero branch retains every compatible urn with stopping count zero.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h m : ℕ} (x : Fin h → ℕ) (hfeas : ∃ N r, m ≤ N ∧ r ≤ m ∧ ∀ i, Compatible N m r (x i)) : ∃ N r, m ≤ N ∧ r ≤ m ∧ (∀ i, Compatible N m r (x i)) ∧ ∀ M s, m ≤ M → s ≤ m → (∀ i, Compatible M m s (x i)) → totalLikelihood x M m s ≤ totalLikelihood x N m r

statement: At fixed population and positive stopping count the complete set of maximizers is the first crossing and its successor precisely on equality. If there is no crossing, the last feasible composition is the sole fit.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h N r : ℕ} (hh : 0 < h) (x : Fin h → ℕ) (hr : 0 < r) (hx : ∀ i, r ≤ x i) (hfeas : ∃ m, ∀ i, Compatible N m r (x i)) : let u := N - maxBlackDraws (fun i ↦ x i-r) let D := Icc r u ∃ b ∈ D, (b < u → compositionRatio x N r b ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ j ∈ Ico r u, j < b → 1 < compositionRatio x N r j) ∧ ∀ j ∈ D, IsMaxOn (fun m ↦ totalLikelihood x N m r) D j ↔ j = b ∨ (j = b+1 ∧ b < u ∧ compositionRatio x N r b = 1)
dossier_scope_note: Positive branch. The separate zero-stopping flatness theorem applies on zeros.

statement: At held population and composition on positive data the first nonpositive ratio crossing identifies every winning stopping count, including an adjacent tie and the terminal-size case.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {h N m : ℕ} (hh : 0 < h) (x : Fin h → ℕ) (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) (hfeas : ∃ r, ∀ i, Compatible N m r (x i)) : let l := max 1 (Finset.univ.sup x-(N-m)) let u := min m (Finset.univ.inf' ⟨⟨0,hh⟩,Finset.mem_univ _⟩ x) let D := Icc l u ∃ b ∈ D, (b < u → stoppingRatio x N m b ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ j ∈ Ico l u, j < b → 1 < stoppingRatio x N m j) ∧ ∀ j ∈ D, IsMaxOn (fun r ↦ totalLikelihood x N m r) D j ↔ j = b ∨ (j = b+1 ∧ b < u ∧ stoppingRatio x N m b = 1)
dossier_scope_note: Positive branch. The zero branch forces stopping count zero by compatibility.

statement: A held interior probability has exactly one maximizer over nonnegative size, with optimum zero on all-zero data. Probability one is compatible only with zeros, for which the entire size ray maximizes.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) {p : ℝ} (hp : p ∈ Ioc 0 1) : ((∀ i, x i = 0) → ∀ r ∈ Ici (0 : ℝ), IsMaxOn (fun s ↦ likelihood x s p) (Ici 0) r ↔ r = 0 ∨ p = 1) ∧ ((¬ ∀ i, x i = 0) → (p < 1 → ∃! r, r ∈ Ici (0 : ℝ) ∧ IsMaxOn (fun s ↦ likelihood x s p) (Ici 0) r) ∧ (p = 1 → ∀ r, likelihood x r p = 0))

statement: At held positive size the fitted probability is unique, including probability one on all-zero data. At size zero only zero data are compatible and all admissible probabilities maximize.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) : ((∀ i, x i = 0) → ∀ p ∈ Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, IsMaxOn (likelihood x r) (Ioc 0 1) p ↔ r = 0 ∨ p = 1) ∧ ((¬ ∀ i, x i = 0) → (0 < r → prob x r ∈ Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ ∀ p ∈ Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, IsMaxOn (likelihood x r) (Ioc 0 1) p ↔ p = prob x r) ∧ (r = 0 → ∀ p, likelihood x r p = 0))

statement: At any feasible trial size, the likelihood is bounded by one. On a nonempty constant sample all saturated parameters are exactly the size-zero fiber or the matching endpoint atom at positive size.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {N n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (c : Fin (N+1)) {p : ℝ} (_hp : p ∈ Icc 0 1) (ν : ℝ) : closedLikelihood (fun _ : Fin n ↦ c) p ν ≤ 1 ∧ (closedLikelihood (fun _ : Fin n ↦ c) p ν = 1 ↔ N = 0 ∨ (p = 0 ∧ c.val = 0) ∨ (p = 1 ∧ c.val = N))
dossier_scope_note: Constant branch of the all-free maximizer-set claim.

statement: Holding probability and dispersion reduces the fit to exact comparison of a finite compatible grid. Every size tied for the best height maximizes.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n B : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℕ) (p ν : ℝ) : let D : Set ℕ := {N | N ≤ B ∧ Compatible x N p} D.Finite ∧ (D.Nonempty ↔ ∃ N ∈ D, IsMaxOn (fun J ↦ sizeLikelihood x J p ν) D N)

statement: At zero dispersion and held interior probability, the smallest compatible size is the sole maximizer over the capped trial-size domain.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n B : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) {p : ℝ} (hp : p ∈ Ioo 0 1) (hB : ∀ i, x i ≤ B) : let D : Set ℕ := {N | N ≤ B ∧ Compatible x N p} ∀ N ∈ D, IsMaxOn (fun J ↦ sizeLikelihood x J p 0) D N ↔ N = Finset.univ.sup x

statement: A positive fixed size has exactly one fitted probability at any held finite dispersion. The endpoint fits are included. Size zero is flat.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {N n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → Fin (N+1)) (ν : ℝ) : (N = 0 → ∀ p ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, closedLikelihood x p ν = 1) ∧ (0 < N → ∃! p, p ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ IsMaxOn (fun q ↦ closedLikelihood x q ν) (Icc 0 1) p)

statement: At held dispersion, the closed probability profiles each attain and a finite comparison over the capped trial designs gives a global fit.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n B : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) (ν : ℝ) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ B) : let D : Set (ℕ × ℝ) := {q | q.1 ≤ B ∧ (∀ i, x i ≤ q.1) ∧ q.2 ∈ Icc 0 1} ∃ q ∈ D, IsMaxOn (fun q ↦ sizeLikelihood x q.1 q.2 ν) D q

statement: Zero dispersion and at least one positive count force the smallest compatible size, even when probability is optimized.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n B : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) (hx : ∃ i, 0 < x i) : let D : Set (ℕ × ℝ) := {q | q.1 ≤ B ∧ (∀ i, x i ≤ q.1) ∧ q.2 ∈ Icc 0 1} ∀ q ∈ D, IsMaxOn (fun t ↦ sizeLikelihood x t.1 t.2 0) D q → q.1 = Finset.univ.sup x

statement: Mixed binary observations have exactly the capped size-one Bernoulli maximizers, with dispersion arbitrary.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n B : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ 1) (hz : ∃ i, x i = 0) (ho : ∃ i, x i = 1) (hB : 1 ≤ B) : let z := (Finset.univ.filter fun i ↦ x i = 0).card let o := (Finset.univ.filter fun i ↦ x i = 1).card let D : Set (ℕ × ℝ × ℝ) := {q | q.1 ≤ B ∧ q.2.1 ∈ Icc 0 1} ∀ q ∈ D, IsMaxOn (fun q ↦ sizeLikelihood x q.1 q.2.1 q.2.2) D q ↔ q.1 = 1 ∧ q.2.1 = (o : ℝ)/(o+z)
dossier_scope_note: Includes the whole dispersion fiber at size one.

statement: Every admissible held dispersion, including zero on the geometric chart, has a unique maximizing rate.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) {ν : ℝ} (hν : 0 ≤ ν) : let D := {r : ℝ | (r,ν) ∈ CMP.rateDomain} ∃! r, r ∈ D ∧ IsMaxOn (fun q ↦ CMP.likelihood x q ν) D r

statement: All zeros attain exactly on the zero-rate fiber. Any sample supported on adjacent cells and containing a positive count has an excluded supremum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) : ((∀ i, x i = 0) → ∀ p ∈ CMP.rateDomain, IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ CMP.likelihood x q.1 q.2) CMP.rateDomain p ↔ p.1 = 0) ∧ ((∃ i, x i ≠ 0) → (∃ c, ∀ i, x i = c ∨ x i = c+1) → ¬ ∃ p ∈ CMP.rateDomain, IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ CMP.likelihood x q.1 q.2) CMP.rateDomain p)
dossier_scope_note: Covers all zeros and adjacent-supported nonzero data. The remaining attainment branch is separate.

statement: The exposed adjacent-cell ray has a two-point limiting distribution. Its two positive masses are proportional to the base weights on those cells.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (c : ℕ) (η : ℝ) (k : ℕ) : let s := log ((c : ℝ)+1) Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ CMP.likelihood (fun _ : Fin 1 ↦ k) (exp (η+t*s)) (1+t)) atTop (𝓝 ((if k ∈ ({c,c+1} : Finset ℕ) then CMP.weight η 1 k else 0) / (CMP.weight η 1 c + CMP.weight η 1 (c+1))))
dossier_scope_note: Pointwise path for the adjacent law, with its two masses expressed as normalized base weights.

statement: A ray with slope strictly between the two adjacent supporting slopes concentrates at the positive count between them.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (c : ℕ) (hc : 0 < c) (k : ℕ) : let s := (log (c : ℝ)+log ((c : ℝ)+1))/2 Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ CMP.likelihood (fun _ : Fin 1 ↦ k) (exp (t*s)) (1+t)) atTop (𝓝 (if k = c then 1 else 0))

statement: With the second rate held, positive values admit a unique first rate. At zero, precisely the nonnegative signed samples admit a unique fit. Any negative observation forces likelihood zero throughout that fiber.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℤ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) : ((0 < r ∨ ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i) → ∃! v, v ∈ Ici 0 ∧ IsMaxOn (fun w ↦ likelihood x (w,r)) (Ici 0) v) ∧ (r = 0 → (∃ i, x i < 0) → ∀ v, likelihood x (v,r) = 0)

statement: Reflection transfers the held-rate result to the first rate. At zero the admissible signed counts are nonpositive.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℤ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) : ((0 < r ∨ ∀ i, x i ≤ 0) → ∃! v, v ∈ Ici 0 ∧ IsMaxOn (fun w ↦ likelihood x (r,w)) (Ici 0) v) ∧ (r = 0 → (∃ i, 0 < x i) → ∀ v, likelihood x (r,v) = 0)

statement: Every nonempty constant Skellam sample has a unique maximizing pair. The compatible Poisson axis supplies the fit, including the origin for zero.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (c : ℤ) : ∃! p, p ∈ domain ∧ IsMaxOn (likelihood (fun _ : Fin n ↦ c)) domain p
dossier_scope_note: Also joined with the one-magnitude branch in joint_unique_at_stated_scope.

statement: The proved all-free uniqueness scopes are constants and mean-zero samples supported on both signs of one positive magnitude.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℤ) (hx : (∃ c, ∀ i, x i = c) ∨ (∃ k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ (∀ i, x i = (k : ℤ) ∨ x i = -(k : ℤ)) ∧ (∑ i, x i = 0) ∧ (∃ i, 0 < x i) ∧ ∃ i, x i < 0)) : ∃! p, p ∈ domain ∧ IsMaxOn (likelihood x) domain p

statement: With alpha held, beta tending to zero gives the upper atom, and beta tending to infinity gives the lower atom.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {m n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℕ) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ m) {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) : Tendsto (likelihood m x a) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (if ∀ i, x i = m then 1 else 0)) ∧ Tendsto (likelihood m x a) atTop (𝓝 (if ∀ i, x i = 0 then 1 else 0))

statement: At held positive alpha and size, exactly the two endpoint-constant samples fail to attain. Each such sample has supremum one and strict inequality at finite beta. At size zero beta is arbitrary.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {m n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ m) {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) : (m = 0 → ∀ b > 0, likelihood m x a b = 1) ∧ (0 < m → ((∃ b ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ), IsMaxOn (likelihood m x a) (Ioi 0) b) ↔ (¬ ∀ i, x i = 0) ∧ (¬ ∀ i, x i = m)) ∧ (((∀ i, x i = 0) ∨ (∀ i, x i = m)) → IsLUB (likelihood m x a '' Ioi 0) 1 ∧ ∀ b > 0, likelihood m x a b < 1))
dossier_scope_note: The attained positive-size maximizer is not shown unique here.

statement: Holding beta at known size gives the reflected criterion, with the same size-zero flat branch and excluded endpoint-constant suprema.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {m n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ m) {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b) : (m = 0 → ∀ a > 0, likelihood m x a b = 1) ∧ (0 < m → ((∃ a ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ), IsMaxOn (fun t ↦ likelihood m x t b) (Ioi 0) a) ↔ (¬ ∀ i, x i = 0) ∧ (¬ ∀ i, x i = m)) ∧ (((∀ i, x i = 0) ∨ (∀ i, x i = m)) → IsLUB ((fun t ↦ likelihood m x t b) '' Ioi 0) 1 ∧ ∀ a > 0, likelihood m x a b < 1))
dossier_scope_note: The attained positive-size maximizer is not shown unique here.

statement: At positive held trial size, sending both shapes to zero at fixed interior mixing mean leaves only the two endpoint atoms.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {m k : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (hk : k ≤ m) {p : ℝ} (hp : p ∈ Ioo 0 1) : Tendsto (fun s : ℝ ↦ mass m k (p*s) ((1-p)*s)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (if k = 0 then 1-p else if k = m then p else 0))

statement: On all-zero data the likelihood is strictly below one at every positive triple. Each of the three free-coordinate routes reaches one.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) (hx : ∀ i, x i = 0) {r a b : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) : exp (logLikelihood x r a b) < 1 ∧ Tendsto (fun t ↦ exp (logLikelihood x t a b)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1) ∧ Tendsto (fun t ↦ exp (logLikelihood x r a t)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1) ∧ Tendsto (fun t ↦ exp (logLikelihood x r t b)) atTop (𝓝 1)
dossier_scope_note: Sample likelihood convergence on zero data. Pointwise mass convergence on positive observations is separate.

statement: At any positive held alpha, a finite joint size and beta fit exists exactly when a positive count occurs.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) : (∃ p ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ) ×ˢ Ioi 0, IsMaxOn (fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ logLikelihood x p.1 a p.2) (Ioi 0 ×ˢ Ioi 0) p) ↔ ∃ i, 0 < x i

statement: All-zero data have a strictly unattained supremum over every positive triple, with a feasible path shrinking size alone.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) (hx : ∀ i, x i = 0) : let D := Ioi (0 : ℝ) ×ˢ Ioi 0 ×ˢ Ioi 0 let L := fun p : ℝ × ℝ × ℝ ↦ exp (logLikelihood x p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2) IsLUB (L '' D) 1 ∧ ∀ p ∈ D, L p < 1
dossier_scope_note: Zero-data branch of the all-free failure claim.

statement: The compact chart covers exactly all nonnegative physical shapes.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 < μ) : BijOn (shape μ) (Ioc 0 1) (Ici 0)

statement: On positive data, the held-mean fit exists exactly at positive variance excess. Whenever it exists it is unique. Otherwise the normalized Poisson height strictly exceeds all finite profiles.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) (hx : ∃ i, 0 < x i) {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 < μ) : let m := (∑ i, (x i : ℝ))/(n : ℝ) let v := (∑ i, ((x i : ℝ)-m)^2)/(n : ℝ) if m < v+(m-μ)^2 then ∃! w, w ∈ Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ IsMaxOn (normalizedProfile x μ) (Ioc 0 1) w else IsLUB (normalizedProfile x μ '' Ioc 0 1) 1 ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, normalizedProfile x μ w < 1
dossier_scope_note: Positive sample branch in the compact shape chart. The physical shape chart bijection is separate.

statement: With positive mean held on zero data, the shape-zero member is the unique fit on the nonnegative shape domain.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {μ : ℝ} (hμ : 0 < μ) {lam : ℝ} (hlam : 0 ≤ lam) : IsMaxOn (HeldSweepPIG.zeroLikelihood n μ) (Ici 0) lam ↔ lam = 0

statement: Positive held shape has a unique mean on positive data. All-zero data approach the excluded zero-mean atom.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) {lam : ℝ} (hlam : 0 < lam) : let f := JoinsPIG.heldShapeLikelihood x lam ((∃ i, 0 < x i) → ∃! μ, μ ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ) ∧ IsMaxOn f (Ioi 0) μ) ∧ ((∀ i, x i = 0) → Tendsto f (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1) ∧ IsLUB (f '' Ioi 0) 1 ∧ ∀ μ > 0, f μ < 1)
dossier_scope_note: Positive held shape only. The zero-shape likelihood is flat in mean on compatible zeros.

statement: A constant sample or a sample occupying two adjacent cells has an unattained saturated supremum. The two-cell height uses its empirical split.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) : let L := {v | ∃ a > 0, ∃ r > 0, likelihood x a r = v} ((∃ j, ∀ i, x i = j) → IsLUB L 1 ∧ ∀ a > 0, ∀ r > 0, likelihood x a r < 1) ∧ (∀ j, (∀ i, x i = j ∨ x i = j+1) → (∃ i, x i = j) → (∃ i, x i = j+1) → let m := (Finset.univ.filter fun i ↦ x i = j).card let k := (Finset.univ.filter fun i ↦ x i ≠ j).card let w := (m : ℝ)/(m+k) IsLUB L (w^m*(1-w)^k) ∧ ∀ a > 0, ∀ r > 0, likelihood x a r < w^m*(1-w)^k)

statement: At fixed location strictly inside cell `j`, shrinking scale concentrates at `j`, with every other cell probability tending to zero.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (j k : ℤ) {m : ℝ} (h₁ : (j : ℝ) < m) (h₂ : m < (j : ℝ)+1) : Tendsto (cell k m) atTop (𝓝 (if k = j then 1 else 0))

statement: Sending inverse scale to infinity and setting the mean at the shared boundary minus `t/B` gives masses `Φ t` and `1 - Φ t` on the adjacent cells.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (j k : ℤ) (t : ℝ) : Tendsto (fun B : ℝ ↦ cell k ((j : ℝ)+1-t/B) B) atTop (𝓝 (if k = j then Φ t else if k = j+1 then 1-Φ t else 0))

statement: With positive scale held, either location escape makes the entire sample likelihood tend to zero.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℤ) {B : ℝ} (hB : 0 < B) : Tendsto (fun m ↦ heldLocationLikelihood x m B) atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ Tendsto (fun m ↦ heldLocationLikelihood x m B) atBot (𝓝 0)

statement: Any attained held-location maximum of the normalized working likelihood is unique.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℤ) (m : ℝ) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hma : IsMaxOn (fun B ↦ workingLikelihood x (m*B,B)) (Ioi 0) a) (hmb : IsMaxOn (fun B ↦ workingLikelihood x (m*B,B)) (Ioi 0) b) : a = b
dossier_scope_note: Uniqueness for an attained fit in the normalized working model.

statement: Any attained held-positive-scale maximum of the normalized working likelihood is unique.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℤ) {B : ℝ} (hB : 0 < B) {a b : ℝ} (ha : IsMaxOn (fun A ↦ workingLikelihood x (A,B)) univ a) (hb : IsMaxOn (fun A ↦ workingLikelihood x (A,B)) univ b) : a = b
dossier_scope_note: Uniqueness for an attained fit in the normalized working model.

statement: The all-free constant or adjacent two-cell data have saturated heights that every finite normal fit strictly misses.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℤ) : let Y := workingLikelihood x '' workingDomain ((∃ j, ∀ i, x i = j) → IsLUB Y 1 ∧ ∀ p ∈ workingDomain, workingLikelihood x p < 1) ∧ (∀ j, (∀ i, x i = j ∨ x i = j+1) → 0 < cellCount x j → 0 < cellCount x (j+1) → let C := adjacentHeight (cellCount x j) (cellCount x (j+1)) IsLUB Y C ∧ ∀ p ∈ workingDomain, workingLikelihood x p < C)

statement: Holding probability fixed on a binary sample with a positive count gives a strict excluded Bernoulli supremum at infinite shape.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℕ) (a : ℝ) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ 1) (hp : ∃ i, x i = 1) : let L := fun β ↦ likelihood x (a,β) let U := ∏ i, if x i = 0 then 1-exp (-exp a) else exp (-exp a) Tendsto L atTop (𝓝 U) ∧ IsLUB (L '' Ioi 0) U ∧ ∀ β > 0, L β < U

statement: Holding shape fixed on an all-zero sample gives the strict excluded zero atom as the survival probability tends to zero.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) (hx : ∀ i, x i = 0) (β : ℝ) (_hβ : 0 < β) : let L := fun a ↦ likelihood x (a,β) Tendsto L atTop (𝓝 1) ∧ IsLUB (range L) 1 ∧ ∀ a, L a < 1

statement: With free probability and shape, holding the collapse location inside a positive cell gives its point mass. At a zero common count the fixed-shape zero-probability path supplies the atom.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (j k : ℕ) {c : ℝ} (h₁ : (j : ℝ) < c) (h₂ : c < (j : ℝ)+1) : Tendsto (fun β : ℝ ↦ mass k (-β*log c,β)) atTop (𝓝 (if k = j then 1 else 0)) ∧ (j = 0 → ∀ β > 0, Tendsto (fun a : ℝ ↦ mass k (a,β)) atTop (𝓝 (if k = 0 then 1 else 0)))
dossier_scope_note: The chart uses a = log(-log q). The zero branch uses a fixed positive shape.
